statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an open subscheme and p a natural number. For module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], restriction along U.ι [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] followed by module cohomology on U [pqf-def-cohomology] and forgetting the global scalar action is naturally isomorphic to openModuleCohomology X p U [def-sc-open-module-cohomology]. No nonemptiness, affine, properness, or positive-degree hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Restrict an injective resolution termwise. Exact open restriction preserves the augmented quasi-isomorphism, and its exact left adjoint implies that restricted terms are injective. Transport through overEquiv U and overFunctorEquiv U to obtain a concrete resolution on the open subscheme; its augmentation in degree zero is the restriction of the original augmentation.

Use restrictAppIso at the terminal open to compare the two section complexes naturally. Exact scalar forgetting commutes with homology. Compose these isomorphisms with isoRightDerivedObj for the two resolutions. For every lift of a coefficient map, naturality of the section-complex isomorphism and the two isoRightDerivedObj formulas gives the naturality square. Choose Mathlib injective resolutions to make a natural isomorphism and invert it to get the orientation in the statement. The proof is implemented completely, including empty opens and degree zero.

theorem nonempty_openRestriction_moduleCohomology_iso
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens) (p : ℕ) :
    Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι ⋙
      RingedSpace.moduleCohomology U.toScheme.toRingedSpace p ⋙
        forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u}
          ((moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)))
            AddCommGrpCat.{u}) ≅
      RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p U)
